rules.statement: Every execution-time filesystem write MUST resolve within the bound repository root. A write whose resolved target lies outside that root MUST be refused before any mutation occurs, and the refusal MUST name this rule.
rules.rationale: ADR-097 D2 makes FileHandler the single write chokepoint; ADR-159 (Note 2026-09-05) requires physical containment of an externally bound run to the materialized copy. Until this rule existed the refusal was real (FileHandler._resolve_repo_path raised a bare ValueError) but unnamed: no rule document stated the obligation, so nothing could be attested to it and a probe recording the refusal had no rule id to cite (#895 D2, governor ruling 2026-09-15). Enforcement is the runtime refusal itself -- passive_gate, attestation class A -- because the property is not statically decidable: which paths a run will attempt is only known when it attempts them. The refusal is typed (RepositoryBoundaryViolationError, a ValueError subclass) and carries rule_id, attempted_path and bound_root so ADR-159 I-5 probe evidence is structured, not parsed from a message. Complements ActionExecutor's physical-containment check, which guards symlink escapes under an authorized prefix inside the copy; this rule binds the boundary of the copy itself.
